tasks.details: Use the .NET CLI to create a new solution file. Create projects for each layer defined in the PRD: Api, BuildingBlocks/Core, BuildingBlocks/Application, BuildingBlocks/Infrastructure, BuildingBlocks/Web, and the first business module Modules/Identity. Configure project references to enforce Clean Architecture dependencies (e.g., Application depends on Domain, Infrastructure depends on Application). Use .NET 10 preview SDK. Set up basic service registration in the Api project's Program.cs for FastEndpoints and MediatR.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the solution builds successfully. Check that project references are correctly configured and that there are no circular dependencies. Run `dotnet build` and ensure it completes without errors. Confirm the project structure matches the PRD exactly.
tasks.title: Establish Solution Structure and Core Project Scaffolding
tasks.description: Initialize the solution and project structure according to the PRD, establishing the foundational layers and projects for the modular monolith. This includes setting up Api, BuildingBlocks, and Modules directories and projects.

tasks.details: In `BuildingBlocks/Core/Functional`, implement `Result<T>` and `Option<T>` types to handle operations that can fail or return nothing, avoiding exceptions for control flow. In `BuildingBlocks/Core/Types`, create a generic record `public record StrongId<T>(Guid Value)` to be used for all entity IDs. In `BuildingBlocks/Core/Domain`, define base classes `Entity<TId>` and `AggregateRoot<TId>` that include common properties like Id, domain events, and basic equality comparison.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests using xUnit for the Result<T> and Option<T> types to validate their monadic behavior (map, bind, etc.). Write unit tests for the StrongId<T> to ensure type safety and proper value handling. Test the base Entity and AggregateRoot classes for correct ID management and domain event handling.
tasks.title: Implement Core Domain Primitives and Functional Patterns
tasks.description: Implement the core domain primitives and functional constructs within the BuildingBlocks/Core project. This includes creating the Result<T> pattern for error handling, a StrongId<T> generic record for type-safe identifiers, and base classes for entities and aggregates.

tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the User aggregate's business logic (e.g., a new user has a `UserRegistered` domain event). Write unit tests for the MediatR handlers using NSubstitute to mock repositories and other dependencies. Ensure validation rules are tested for the `RegisterUserCommand`.
tasks.details: In `Modules/Identity/Domain`, define the `User` aggregate root with properties like `UserId` (using `StrongId<User>`), `Email`, `PasswordHash`. Encapsulate business logic for registration and password management within the aggregate, raising domain events like `UserRegistered`. In `Modules/Identity/Application`, create MediatR commands like `RegisterUserCommand` and `LoginQuery`. Implement corresponding handlers that load the `User` aggregate, execute domain logic, and persist changes using a repository interface (`IUserRepository`). Use FluentValidation to validate incoming requests.
tasks.title: Develop Identity Module: Domain and Application Layers
tasks.description: Develop the domain and application layers for the Identity module, including the User aggregate, domain events, and CQRS commands/queries for user registration and authentication.

tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests using Testcontainers to spin up a real PostgreSQL database. The test should send a request to the registration endpoint, then query the database to verify the user was created correctly. Use FluentAssertions to validate the API response. Test error paths, such as registering with a duplicate email.
tasks.description: Implement the infrastructure and API layers for the Identity module. This includes setting up EF Core persistence for the User aggregate and exposing user management functionality via FastEndpoints.
tasks.details: In `Modules/Identity/Infrastructure`, implement `IUserRepository` using EF Core 9. Create an `EntityTypeConfiguration` for the `User` aggregate, mapping it to a PostgreSQL table and configuring the `StrongId` to `Guid` conversion. In the `Api/Endpoints/Identity` folder, create a `RegisterUserEndpoint` using FastEndpoints. This endpoint will map the incoming HTTP request to the `RegisterUserCommand`, send it via MediatR, and return a JWT token upon success or a Problem Details response on failure.
tasks.title: Implement Identity Module: Infrastructure and API Layers

tasks.description: Set up and configure the core observability and testing infrastructure for the application. This involves integrating OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing and establishing a robust framework for integration testing.
tasks.details: In the `Api` project, configure OpenTelemetry to trace incoming requests, MediatR command/query pipelines, and EF Core database calls. Export traces to the console or a collector. In the `tests` directory, create a base class for integration tests (`BaseIntegrationTest`). This class should handle setting up Testcontainers for PostgreSQL, managing database state (e.g., resetting between tests), and providing a pre-configured `HttpClient` for making API calls.
tasks.title: Configure Observability and Testing Infrastructure
tasks.testStrategy: Validate that distributed traces are generated correctly by running an integration test for the user registration endpoint and inspecting the console output for trace information. Confirm that the integration test base class successfully starts and stops the PostgreSQL container. Write a simple health check endpoint and a corresponding integration test to verify the testing infrastructure is working.
